ratingNotes: Largest Sub-Saharan African economy. Oil export revenue dependency creates fiscal volatility. Security challenges in Niger Delta and North-East. Governance reform progress under current administration. IMF article IV 2024 completed.

Post-Tigray Peace Agreement (Nov 2022) economic recovery underway. IMF ECF program signed 2023 ($3.4B). Debt restructuring with Paris Club creditors in progress. Significant humanitarian needs and displacement still affecting fiscal space.

Stable political environment post-2022 elections. Elevated debt service burden — external debt service approaching 30% of revenues. Digital economy and M-Pesa ecosystem advantage. IMF ECF/EFF extended 2021. Strong remittance inflows from diaspora.

Stable macro environment under President Hassan. Natural gas export revenues diversifying commodity base. Tourism recovery post-COVID contributing to FX. Debt levels manageable. Human development indicators improving but still low.

Fragile and conflict-affected state (FCS). Active armed conflict in North Kivu (M23, FDLR) and Ituri regions. High aid dependency (~$4B annual ODA). Cobalt/copper mining revenues partially offset by governance weakness and infrastructure gaps. IDA FCS premium protocols apply.

Debt restructuring 2022-2023 completed via IMF ECF ($3B) and Paris Club agreement. Domestic debt exchange programme (DDEP) implemented. Cocoa and gold export recovery improving external position. Post-restructuring stabilisation — enhanced scrutiny on new borrowings per IDA 21 debt limit framework.

First sub-Saharan African country to default in COVID era (Nov 2020). IMF ECF programme completed 2023. Eurobond restructuring finalised 2024. AgriConnect digital agriculture programme expected to boost rural GDP by 1.5-2% p.a. Copper price recovery improving fiscal outlook.

Strong export growth driven by ready-made garment (RMG) sector ($47B exports 2023). Fastest-growing South Asian economy. Climate vulnerability — cyclone and flood risk affecting 40M coastal residents. Remittance flows ($22B) provide FX buffer. IDA graduation pathway active.

Investment grade sovereign. 4th most populous nation (277M). Nickel, palm oil, and coal export revenues diversifying. New capital Nusantara infrastructure drive. Prudent fiscal management — debt below 40% GDP. New capital city development and green transition creating IBRD pipeline.

Upper-middle income with large domestic capital market. Lula administration (2023-) reversing Amazon deforestation — positive ESG signal for international capital. High public debt but largely domestically financed. Agricultural powerhouse — soy, beef, and sugarcane exports. Amazon deforestation down 50% in 2023.

Investment grade. World's most populous country (1.4B). Fastest-growing major economy (7%+ GDP growth 2023-24). Largest single IBRD+IDA blend borrower by portfolio size. Infrastructure investment supercycle driving IBRD demand. Digital public infrastructure (UPI, Aadhaar, ONDC) as global model. Debt primarily domestic.

Near-default 2023 — averted by IMF Stand-By Arrangement ($3B SBA, Jul 2023). Energy sector circular debt (~PKR 2.4T) remains critical risk. Political instability post-2023 elections. Severe FX reserve depletion in 2022-23. IMF programme compliance improving. Energy sector transformation critical to fiscal stabilisation.
